thaw_line: Something in the world gave way, just a little.
The air in the region changed, and everyone felt it.
It was a small change, but it was the right sort of change.
thaw_line@lantern: All across the region it began to drip, a single drop from the end of one icicle.
The snow turned to slush, and the slush to rain, and the rain was warm.
Where the seal had broken, the ice cracked from end to end with a sound like a river stretching.
Small green things pushed up through the slush as though they had been waiting behind a door.
thaw_line@returner: For the first time, the morning came differently, and {w1} noticed at once.
Something unfamiliar happened: a bird sang a note {w1} had not heard before.
The day went off the old script, and {w1} nearly wept with relief.
thaw_line@overlord: A cold draught ran through the black glass halls, and the clerks looked up from their ledgers.
In the demon realm a lantern went out, one of the ones that had never gone out.
Somewhere a bell rang in the castle that nobody had been told to ring.
thaw_line@slime: The harvest came in a little fuller that week, and the market stalls remembered colours.
Prices fell, tempers softened, and somebody put out a second chair.
The road to town was a little busier the next morning, with fewer worried faces.
thaw_line@shield: A few shutters opened in the street, and a few faces looked out for the first time in weeks.
People stopped crossing the road. Not all of them, but some.
The whispering, for an afternoon, went quiet, as if it had lost its place.
thaw_line@gate: In every Status Window, a grey line of text became a little less grey.
The Rule loosened by one notch, and every Chog felt it in their bones.
A floor of the sky unlocked, and light came through the crack.
thaw_line@misfits: Against every reasonable expectation, things went to plan, which alarmed everyone.
Nothing caught fire. A new record was declared.
The wall held. Nobody could say exactly why, and nobody was inclined to ask.
thaw_line@hidden: The Quest log chimed, and a line of text turned gold.
A new door opened in the sky, a polite one, with a number on it.
The stars rearranged themselves a little, like people shuffling along a bench.

closing: It was not the end of anything. It was the middle of everything.
And so it began, and so it went on.
They did not know it yet, but the story had already turned.
Nobody said so aloud, but everyone felt it.
The night went on, as nights do.
closing@lantern: Outside, the snow kept falling, softer than before.
Somewhere beyond the hill, something silver paused, and listened, and went on.
The lantern burned all night, though nobody had lit it.
closing@returner: {w1} would remember this, whatever came next. That, at least, was a comfort.
The day ended, and for once {w1} did not know what the next one held.
It was the first time in a long while that the evening had not been a rehearsal.
closing@overlord: In the castle, someone made a note in a ledger and underlined it twice.
The Demon King sipped cold tea and said nothing for a long while.
A very small imp wrote it all down, in case it mattered.
closing@slime: It was not much, but it was theirs.
Somebody lit a second lamp, for no reason except that it was nice.
The town went to sleep a little larger than it had woken.
closing@shield: {w1} did not defend themselves. They went on, doing the next honest thing.
The whispers went on, but so did {w1}.
Truth is slow, but it has long legs.
closing@gate: In the sky, the grey numbers ticked down by one.
The Rule did not blink. Neither did they.
A little more of the map turned from black to gold.
closing@misfits: Nobody could have planned it, and nobody tried.
The goose, at least, was proud.
They agreed never to speak of it. They told everyone.
closing@hidden: Quietly, in the dark, a line of gold text added itself to the log.
A star, very high up, winked once.
The Quest did not say well done. It never did. It just offered the next one.
